title: FCA warns AI may reveal more cyber vulnerabilities firms can cope with
source_used: Compliance Week (first two paragraphs; rest behind registration)
key_facts: The UK Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) warned that rapid AI development is exposing weaknesses in financial firms' cybersecurity because existing controls cannot keep pace with risks new technology creates or exploits.
In a review, the FCA said frontier AI models, the most advanced models available at a time, can help firms find and analyse their own vulnerabilities faster.
The same models, if used maliciously, amplify cyber threats to firms' safety and soundness, customers, market integrity and financial stability, the FCA said.
Article by Neil Hodge, Compliance Week, published 3 Oct 2026.
quote_evidence: The UK's financial regulator has warned that the rapid pace of AI development is revealing vulnerabilities in firms' cybersecurity arrangements because their existing controls cannot keep up with the risks new technology can either create or exploit.
"but if used maliciously, amplify cyber threats to firms' safety and soundness, customers, market integrity, and financial stability."
why_it_matters_hint: The UK regulator says AI is finding holes in banks' defences faster than the banks can close them.
